That was very fast (0.25s for 25 cases). So the campaign seeds must have run quickly too. The earlier runs with FUZZ_TRIALS up to 32 were fast because the topologies are small.

Hmm wait, 0.25s for 25 cases with up to 7 nodes? The reference is O(F^2 · deg · trials) — with F≈20 flows, that's small. OK.

Let me run a big campaign synchronously: 500 cases across varied parameters, with larger node counts (up to 10) and trials up to 32.

Let me also make the fuzzer generate more extreme settings: epsilon up to 250000, cutoff/gamma/bias/tau extremes, cache_slots up to 8.

Let me run a large campaign now.

arguments.command: cd /workspace && time (for s in $(seq 200 215); do FUZZ_TRIALS=$(( (s % 4) * 8 + 5 )) FUZZ_NODES=$(( s % 4 + 6 )) FUZZ_DISCONNECTED=$(( s % 2 )) python3 tmp/fuzz.py $s 40 || { echo "FAILED $s"; break; }; done) 2>&1 | tail -20
